##
[0.1.69](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/compare/deepagents-code==0.1.68...deepagents-code==0.1.69)
(2026-09-14)

### Features

- Update `read_file` output formatting.
([#5648](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5648))
- Surface DeepSeek V4.1 Flash in the model picker.
([#6254](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6254))
- Surface locally tracked GitHub stacks in agent context.
([#6290](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6290))
- Copy a model slug with Ctrl+click.
([#6243](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6243))
- Show session length in the Debug Console.
([#6224](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6224))

### Bug Fixes

- Price nested usage with its own model and honor completions.
([#6251](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6251))
- Drop stale Anthropic thinking blocks.
([#6300](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6300))
- Isolate credentials used for user shell tracing.
([#6242](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6242))
- Attribute dotenv configuration sources.
([#6222](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6222))
- Expose unknown reasoning effort values.
([#6241](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6241))
- Open the Debug Console at the bottom of the log.
([#6218](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6218))
- Order Debug Console log filters.
([#6217](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6217))
- Show the spinner during pre-stream turn setup.
([#6253](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6253))
- Demote no-output hint suppression messages to debug logging.
([#6245](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/6245))

_End release notes preview._

appended to the GitHub release notes automatically at publish time (see
[Release
Pipeline](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/main/.github/RELEASING.md#release-pipeline),
step 3).

commit.message:
fix(code): drop stale Anthropic thinking blocks (#6300)

Deep Agents Code now drops stale preserved-thinking blocks instead of
failing when its prompt prefix changes.

---

Claude's preserved-thinking validation rejects earlier thinking blocks
after memory injection or client-side compaction changes their prefix.
Default supported Anthropic models to
`prefix_mismatch_behavior="drop_block"` and add the required beta while
preserving explicit behavior, existing thinking options, and beta
headers.

Made by [Open
SWE](https://openswe.vercel.app/agents/3173fcbc-189d-5473-ac7b-b91c9761be06)
· openai:gpt-5.6-sol (medium)

commit.message:
feat(talon): register chat commands as Discord slash commands (#6303)

## Why

Talon's chat commands are plain message text parsed in `host.py`. Typing
`/` in Discord offered nothing, so users had to already know the
vocabulary. This registers them as native Discord application commands,
so `/help`, `/new`, `/stop` and `/mcp-reload` appear in the `/` picker
with autocomplete and the reply arrives as that command's own response.

## How

An invocation is converted into **the exact `ChannelMessage` a typed
command would have produced** and dispatched through the normal handler.
`host.py` therefore keeps a single command code path and needs no
knowledge of interactions; the adapter adds no second notion of what a
command means.

- **`deepagents_talon/commands.py` (new)** is the single source of
truth. The host derives its dispatch constants and `/help` text from it
(verified byte-for-byte identical to the previous hand-written string),
and the Discord adapter builds registration from the same entries. A
test asserts every registry entry has a host branch, so a command cannot
be advertised in one place and missing from another.
- **Authorization reuses `_allows_discord_message` unchanged.** The
interaction path rebuilds the same three metadata keys with
`from_self=False`; a test asserts the metadata is identical to that of a
typed `/new`. There is no second authorization code path.
- **Reply routing** uses a sink held in a `ContextVar`. `discord.py`
runs every interaction in its own task (`CommandTree._from_interaction`
→ `loop.create_task`), so each invocation sees only its own sink and an
unrelated task — a cron delivery, a background result, a progress
message aimed at the same channel — cannot be captured by one.
- **Sync runs once per process** on first ready, claiming the flag
before awaiting because `on_ready` re-fires on every reconnect. A sync
failure is logged and leaves the channel connected and usable.

`/reset-all-history` is registered as **hidden**: it deletes stored
history irreversibly and Talon has no confirmation step, so an
autocomplete entry is too easy to hit by accident. It still works when
typed. Flipping one flag in the registry would both register it and add
it to `/help`.

## Reviewer notes

Two things worth a look:

1. **Behavior change, deliberate.** Discord requires a response to every
interaction, so an invocation the exposure policy refuses now receives a
brief private refusal, where a typed command is silently dropped. Slash
commands are visible to anyone who can see the bot, so the exposure
policy — not their visibility — is what restricts use. In guilds this
could be narrowed later with `default_member_permissions`; in DMs it
cannot.
2. **Why a `ContextVar` and not a dict keyed by conversation id.** A
table has a real hijack window: `/help` deliberately skips the
conversation lock and `/new`/`/stop` can hold one for up to 30s. I
confirmed this rather than assuming it — swapping the `ContextVar` for a
dict makes `test_concurrent_slash_commands_answer_their_own_interaction`
fail, with the first command's reply going to the second command's
interaction.

New env vars (both optional, prefixed so `_is_runtime_env` keeps them):

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_DISCORD_SLASH_COMMANDS` | `true` | Disable
registration entirely |
| `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_DISCORD_COMMAND_GUILD_ID` | unset | Register in one
guild instantly, for development. Global is the only kind that reaches
DMs |

Registration needs the **`applications.commands`** scope alongside `bot`
in the invite URL; a bot invited with only `bot` still receives messages
but a guild-scoped sync is rejected. Documented in the README.

## Testing

`make lint` and `make test` clean. 1070 passed; the 6
`test_mcp_config.py::test_runtime_gates_real_config_writes` failures are
**pre-existing** — I reproduced them on a clean `origin/main` worktree
(`'ToolCallingModel' object has no attribute 'startswith'`), unrelated
to this change.

- **`tests/unit_tests/test_commands.py`** (new): every name passes
discord.py's own `validate_name`, descriptions fit the 100-char limit,
help text lists visible and omits hidden, and the host's dispatch
constants match the registry.
- **`tests/channels/test_discord.py`**: 30 new tests. Metadata parity
with a typed command; ephemeral refusal without deferring; chunking
across followups; no-reply and failure fallbacks so a deferred
interaction never hangs on "thinking"; a reply to another conversation
going to the channel instead; concurrent interactions each answering
their own. The tree is faked but `app_commands.Command` construction is
real, so name validation and callback-signature extraction are genuinely
exercised.
- **`tests/integration_tests/test_discord_host.py`** (new): drives a
real `TalonHost` from an interaction — `/new` advances the conversation
thread, `/stop` and `/help` reply through the interaction, an
unauthorized invocation never reaches the agent, and an ordinary agent
turn's reply still goes to the channel rather than into an interaction.

Also checked the real `discord.py` payload offline: all four commands
build with `contexts=[0, 1, 2]` (GUILD, BOT_DM, PRIVATE_CHANNEL) and
`integration_types=[0]`, so the payload carries the BOT_DM context that
makes commands visible in operator DMs.

**Still needs a live check before release**, which no offline test can
cover: that Discord actually surfaces guild-install + BOT_DM commands in
the bot's DM. If it does not, the fix is
`AppInstallationType(guild=True, user=True)` plus enabling User Install
in the developer portal.

`openwiki/integrations/talon.md` describes the command set at line 72
and is now slightly stale. I left it alone on purpose — its frontmatter
carries a generated/verified stamp, so hand-editing would falsely claim
tool verification. `host.py` and `README.md` are already listed sources,
so a regeneration picks this up; that regeneration should also add
`commands.py` and `channels/discord.py` to `sources`, since the Discord
adapter is missing from that list today.
